about.title: San Jose Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in San Jose takes many shapes. Some people spend the day on a jobsite off Monterey Road, others drive deliveries along US-101 and I-280, and plenty sit at a desk in a north San Jose office park. An injury can happen in any of those settings, and when it does, the first system most workers encounter is California workers' compensation. That coverage pays medical care and partial wages no matter who was at fault, and in most cases it is the only claim you can bring against your employer. It is not always the whole picture, though. If someone outside your company caused the harm—a subcontractor on the same site, the owner of the building where you were working, the company that built a faulty machine, or another driver on the road while you were on the clock—California allows a separate injury claim against that third party. Sorting out which path applies, or whether both do, is the question an independent San Jose attorney can help you answer. LawProactive makes that introduction for free.

whyChoose.title: Why San Jose Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Third-party claims don't get overlooked
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker or driver can be held responsible separately. The attorneys we connect you with look for that second path.

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from day one
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party injury claim generally must be filed within two years. Getting matched early keeps both clocks in view.

items.title: Retaliation is taken seriously
items.desc: It is illegal for a San Jose employer to fire, demote or cut your hours because you reported an injury or filed a claim. An independent attorney can explain your options if that happens.

items.question: I was rear-ended on US-101 while driving a company van in San Jose. Is that just workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. Since another driver caused the crash, California also lets you pursue a separate injury claim against that driver, and that claim carries a two-year filing deadline. In 2025 San Jose recorded 3,457 injury collisions, so on-the-clock crashes are a routine part of workplace injury cases here.

items.question: I didn't tell my supervisor right away. Have I lost my rights?
items.answer: California asks workers to report an injury to their employer within 30 days, so the sooner you do it the better. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim, but it does not automatically end every option you have. Report it in writing now, keep a copy, and talk to an attorney about where things stand.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me to find a San Jose attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and there is no fee to be matched. The independent attorneys in our network handle injury claims on contingency, which means they are paid only if there is a recovery.
